text:
maria: Quick FYI — after yesterday's kernel/batching push the prefix cache hit-rate dropped ~18% for a subset of tenants. I dug into the logs and found a bunch of cache key collisions across tenants when quantized model flags changed.
aaron: ugh. do you have an example key? can we repro locally?
sasha: tagging in case this touches security/tenant isolation assumptions @olga
mar ia: repro snippet from prod logs (sanitized):
```
cache_key=sha1( prefix_fingerprint + model_name + q8_flag )
stored_value_id=entry_42 tenant_id=tenant_77
cache_key=sha1( prefix_fingerprint + model_name + q4_flag )
stored_value_id=entry_42 tenant_id=tenant_12
```
so same sha1 output used for two tenants because prefix_fingerprint omitted tenant id in older code.
aaron: oof — that would explain cross-tenant reads if lookup didn't include tenant namespace. Did the code path change during the batching kernel swap?
maria: kernel selection patch introduced an optimization that canonicalized prefixes to reduce KV size; during canonicalization we accidentally moved tenant scoping earlier in the pipeline and a fallback path used legacy keying.
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1209 — cache_isolation_regression. Refer to runbook /incidents/cache-isolation.
kevin: immediate mitigation: add tenant_id (or tenant_hmac) to the cache key and roll forward with a fast patch. Also we should invalidate suspected colliding entries.
olga: +1. But we can't just invalidate everything — need to avoid cold-cache meltdown. Suggest: 1) patch to keying to include tenant HMAC (short), 2) start writing new keys only (no immediate deletion), 3) gradually expire old collision-prone namespace via TTL and proactive warmup.
sasha: agree. Also we should encrypt cache values at rest per tenant; even if there was a read, values are stored encrypted with tenant-specific key and KMS access. Does current cache store plaintext?
maria: current Redis cluster stores plaintext (internal only). We already encrypt in Private deployments but hosted used plaintext for perf. That was a conscious trade-off for latency.
kevin: For hosted customers we need a risk assessment. If cross-tenant reads occurred, what's the worst-case? prefixes are prompt fingerprints and partial completions — PII risk is low but not zero. We should run an audit: how many reads were served by entries where lookup tenant != owner_tenant.
aaron: profiling numbers I pasted earlier: before patch hit_rate=62.1% latency=3.2ms per lookup; after kernel swap hit_rate=50.7% latency=3.6ms and collisions_count jumped to ~1.4k/min for the affected pool.
maria: plan: short term (hotfix within 2h): patch keying to include tenant_id -> deploy to edge, route writes to new namespace. mid term (48-72h): background migration process to rekey hot entries with tenant HMAC, prewarm hot prefixes per-tenant from traces. long term: implement encrypted cache entries + audit logs + collision detector.
olga: For the HMAC approach, use per-tenant secret: cache_key = HMAC(tenant_secret, prefix_fingerprint || model || flags) || ':' || model_version. That way collisions across tenants are cryptographically impossible without secret.
kevin: ops concerns: HMAC adds CPU. We measured earlier: HMAC-SHA256 adds ~0.7µs per key on our path — negligible vs network. But need to bench in tight loops. Also storage footprint increases slightly.
aaron: warmup strategy: 1) collect top-1k prefixes per-tenant from last 24h; 2) replay generation to repopulate new namespace with low QPS ramp; 3) use a guided rekeyer that touches only entries with access_count > threshold.
sasha: also add telemetry: tag every cache read with "namespace_version" and record metric cache_namespace_mismatch_count. We need an alert when cross-tenant reads > 0 (for a safety window) and a dashboard showing hit-rate by tenant and by namespace_version.
maria: regression root cause doc: small patch to canonicalization order + missing tenant field in legacy codepath = key collisions. Missed in code review because tests mock single-tenant path. Add unit tests that simulate multi-tenant canonicalization and property tests for key uniqueness.
olga: audit plan: create a read-only query to count possible exposures (reads where lookup_tenant != owner_tenant) using request logs + cache metadata. If exposure count > 0, notify legal and send customer-safe disclosure plan.
kevin: migration caveat: if we start writing new keys only, cold-start will hurt latencies for those tenants. To avoid SLO slippage, add temporary burst capacity and increase batch sizes for affected pools to amortize token cost during warmup.
aaron: quick PR checklist for hotfix: - include tenant_hmac in key - bump namespace_version header - add metric cache_namespace_mismatch_count - temporary sidecar invalidation script (dry-run)
maria: I'll open the PR and coordinate canary rollout to 3 pods. Can someone own the audit query? @olga?
olga: I'll run the audit once hotfix deploys. Also will start drafting the encrypted value design doc.
sasha: Related note: update the docs for private deployments to clarify we already encrypt cache entries and provide migration steps.
kevin: postmortem TODOs: root-cause, timeline, customer impact, mitigation, controls (HMAC, encryption, tests, alerts).
maria: thanks team. I'll post updates here and in INC-2026-1209. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy patch started by maria at 1719854460 to canary pods (3/40).
aaron: canary perf after patch: hit_rate=61.5% (partial), collisions_count ~3/min, avg_lookup=3.25ms. Looks promising.
maria: rolling to remainder — monitoring dashboards now.
olga: audit query queued; will share counts by EOD.
kevin: adding a follow-up to propose encrypted-at-rest for hosted as opt-in first, then opt-out as needed.
sasha: good. Also add an automated property test: generate random tenant ids + prefixes and assert no collisions across 10k draws.
maria: closing loop — we'll keep this thread for notes. If any customer-facing action is needed we'll coordinate with support and legal.
